 This application coming on for hearing this day, the co
 following:
 Order

This petition under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. has been preferred by the petitioners being aggrieved by the penultimate paragraph of the judgment dated 17.03.2008 passed in Criminal Case No.960/96 whereby the private complaint registered under Section 7(2)(3) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 r/w Section 16 (1)( d ) (1) of the said Act against the petitioners and accused S.S. Agarwal was dismissed against accused S.S. Agarwal, Production Manager, SKG Solvex Ltd. as the prosecution could not prove its case beyond reasonable doubts and accordingly, accused S.S.
Agarwal was acquitted.

2. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits though in Para 9 of the said judgment, it has been observed by learned trial Court that there was no sanction given by the Competent Authority as provided under Section 20 of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.

It was also held by learned trial Court that no offence was found proved against the Production Manager but the matter was directed to be kept pending with the tip on the front page of the case that since other co-accused persons are absconding, the record of the case shall not be eliminated.

The case of accused S.S.
Agarwal, Production Manager of the Company and the Directors who are present petitioners
is similar and therefore, deserves to be met with a similar fate.
Since accused S.S. Agarwal has already been acquitted by the trial Court, no purpose would be served in keeping the matter pending treating the petitioners absconding.

It was further submitted that against the order of acquittal, to the best of his knowledge, no appeal has been 3 MCRC-4788-2008 preferred by the State which goes to show that the judgment passed in the matter of accused S.S. Agarwal has been accepted by the State.
Thus, it was prayed that the said observations made in Para 17 of the said judgment be deleted.

3. Per contra, Shri Tiwari though opposes the prayer made by learned counsel for the petitioner but fairly admits that the allegations levelled against accused S.S.Agarwal, Production Manager and the petitioners were same and, to the best of his knowledge, no appeal has been preferred by the State and if this Court, deems it fit, may delete the said observation.
4. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and perusing the record, this Court finds that the case of the petitioner is akin to the case of accused S.S. Agarwal, Production Manager of the Company against whom, the trial was conducted and vide impugned judgment dated 17.02.2008, he was acquitted.

Since no appeal has been preferred by the State against the said judgment of acquittal, this Court finds that no purpose would be served in keeping the matter pending so far as Swaroop Jain vs State Of M.P. on 13 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140191775/

5. Accordingly, the observation made in Para 17 of the impugned judgment passed by learned trial Court is hereby deleted.
6. To the aforesaid extent, present petition stands allowed.
